title: Merge Intervals
description:
Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

Two intervals overlap if they share at least one point; intervals that merely touch, such as [1,4] and [4,5], are considered overlapping and must be merged.

You may return the merged intervals in any order.

examples.explanation: Intervals [1,3] and [2,6] overlap, so they are merged into [1,6].
Intervals [1,4] and [4,5] touch at 4 and are considered overlapping, so they merge into [1,5].

approach: Sorting by start makes all intervals that can extend a merged interval arrive consecutively. If the next start is no greater than the current merged end, update that end to the larger endpoint; otherwise append a new interval. Sorting dominates the time complexity at O(n log n), followed by an O(n) scan. Space is O(n) for the sorted copy and the returned list.
